key_insight: Inherent randomness in autoregressive decoding sets a fundamental error floor for length prediction from prefill hidden states, with tested predictors performing close to that limit.
engineering_relevance: LLM inference schedulers should account for irreducible length uncertainty rather than expect predictor architecture improvements alone to deliver precise forecasts.
method: Model decoding as a stopped stochastic process with a gradually increasing stopping probability.
Derive per-prompt approximate normality, an explicit approximation error, and the affine variability law σ = αμ + b.
Compare MLP, EGTP, FiLM, soft-label, and Mixture-of-Experts predictors under fixed conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the normal approximation reproduces per-prompt MAE and central distribution mass within a few percent, while varied predictors converge to similar near-bound performance under fixed model, data, and sampling conditions.
watch_item: The normal approximation retains mild tail deviations; benchmark comparisons should fix model, data, and sampling parameters and report relative alongside absolute errors.
paper_title: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction
